citing_sentences: As shown in Figure 1(a), our error analysis shows that many failures stem from incorrect observation actions: the model either localizes the wrong region or obtains crops that lack sufficient evidence.

We further find that bounding-box tokens exhibit substantially higher generation entropy than ordinary language tokens, as shown in Figure 1(b), suggesting that visual localization is a high-uncertainty local decision.
As shown in Figure 1(a, top), Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct achieves an answer accuracy of 87.96% on V*.

In the spatial-relation example (Figure 6, top), Qwen3-VL-8B observes both the cone and the baby carriage but fails to reliably resolve their left-right relation; OPO-8B instead crops a local region containing both objects and correctly determines that the carriage is to the right of the cone.

abstract: Complex visual question answering often requires vision-language models to think with images, i.e., actively acquire local visual evidence by zooming into informative regions of high-resolution images. Our error analysis shows that many failures in this setting originate from incorrect observation actions, where the model fails to localize key regions or obtain crops that contain sufficient evidence for answering. We further observe that bounding-box tokens exhibit substantially higher generation entropy than ordinary language tokens, indicating high uncertainty when the model decides where to look. However, existing reinforcement learning methods based on final-answer rewards provide only trajectory-level feedback, making it difficult to assign precise credit to the observation actions. We propose Observation Policy Optimization (OPO), an RL algorithm for optimizing observation actions in tool-augmented thinking with images. OPO consists of two core modules. First, Uncertainty-Guided Observation Branching (UOB) treats each image zoom-in tool call as an observation event and selectively branches at high-uncertainty, low-redundancy events during rollout, enabling efficient exploration of alternative cropping decisions and their resulting visual evidence. Second, Evidence-Localized Advantage Attribution (ELAA) compares sibling branches using local evidence-sufficiency rewards and assigns credit only to the corresponding observation-action tokens. By decoupling observation-action optimization from trajectory-level outcome supervision, OPO improves visual evidence acquisition and further enhances visual reasoning performance. Experiments show that OPO consistently improves Qwen3-VL models across scales and achieves competitive performance against larger models and tool-augmented baselines. Code is publicly available.

sections.body: The introduction frames tool-augmented thinking with images, where a VLM calls a zoom-in tool during multi-turn reasoning. The authors report that many failures come from incorrect observation actions, and that bounding-box tokens have substantially higher generation entropy than ordinary language tokens (Figure 1). Final-answer rewards give imprecise credit to these actions. OPO adds two modules: Uncertainty-Guided Observation Branching (UOB) and Evidence-Localized Advantage Attribution (ELAA). Across V*, HR-Bench 4K and HR-Bench 8K, OPO raises overall accuracy by 10.0, 12.4 and 15.8 percentage points for Qwen3-VL-2B, and by 4.7, 4.1 and 4.3 percentage points for Qwen3-VL-8B. Ablations show that both modules contribute to these gains.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Zoom-in failures mostly stem from observation actions, and OPO adds up to 15.8 points for Qwen3-VL-2B.

sections.body: The related work covers thinking with images. DeepEyes learns a zoom-based observation policy through reinforcement learning, and Thyme uses executable code for image manipulation. DeepEyesV2 and SenseNova-MARS combine visual operations with search, and ZwZ distills region-level supervision for single-pass perception. CodeVision and CodeV use process rewards for code-based tool use. CodeV combines evidence scores with answer correctness into a trajectory-level advantage. The section also covers agentic reinforcement learning, where ARPO and AEPO use token entropy to branch at high-uncertainty tool-call steps. The authors state that OPO specializes this idea to visual observation by exploring alternative crops and attributing feedback to the evidence each crop produces.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Related methods reward crop quality or whole trajectories, whereas OPO compares sibling crops and assigns local credit to observation tokens.

sections.body: Each valid zoom-in tool call is an observation event, and its region-label, bounding-box and image-index tokens are observation-action tokens. On V*, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct reaches 87.96% accuracy, and approximately 74% of its incorrect answers are mainly caused by observation errors. The DeepEyes-trained model reaches 90.05%, yet approximately 79% of its incorrect answers still originate from observation errors. Token entropy is computed per decoding position over the full vocabulary. On V*, bounding-box tokens have mean entropy 0.522 and median entropy 0.501, against 0.229 and 0.225 for reasoning tokens. Answer tokens average 0.006. The authors conclude that visual localization is a high-uncertainty decision.
sections.heading: Preliminary Analysis
sections.headline: Observation errors cause about 74% of Qwen3-VL-8B failures on V*, and box tokens show higher entropy.

sections.body: UOB divides a rollout budget M into B base trajectories and reserves P=M-B slots for branching and backfill. Each base trajectory decodes until its first zoom-in call. UOB scores each event by the mean entropy of its bounding-box tokens plus a weighted standard deviation of that entropy. It normalizes this score against the pre-action entropy baseline for the same question. A child crop is kept only if its overlap with earlier crops in the branch group does not exceed `tau_red`. ELAA has a frozen visual judge label each crop as insufficient, partial or sufficient, mapped to -1, 0 and 1. It normalizes these rewards within each branch group. The local advantage is applied only to image-index, region-label and bounding-box tokens. This section reports no numerical results.
sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: UOB branches at uncertain, non-redundant zoom events, and ELAA gives sibling crops local advantages on observation tokens.

sections.body: Baselines include proprietary models such as GPT-5 mini and Gemini-3 Pro, open-source models such as Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL, and workflow or tool methods such as DeepEyes and ZoomEye. Training runs for 200 iterations on 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs, with 64 prompts per batch, rollout budget M=8 and B=2. Qwen3-VL-2B with OPO reaches 85.9 on V* overall, 78.4 on HR-Bench 4K and 76.4 on HR-Bench 8K. Qwen3-VL-8B with OPO reaches 92.7, 85.5 and 80.8. Each ablation on the 2B model scores below the full method. Setting M=16 with B=2 gives 86.2, 78.8 and 76.9, which the authors describe as marginal gains. OPO-8B's V* score is below Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B at 93.7 in Table 1.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: OPO-8B scores 92.7 on V* and 85.5 on HR-Bench 4K, and every ablated variant trails the full 2B model.

sections.body: The conclusion argues that models must learn where to look, not only how to reason. It reports that failures on high-resolution tasks originate at the observation stage, and that observation-action tokens are more uncertain than language tokens. OPO branches locally at high-uncertainty, low-redundancy events and assigns evidence feedback only to the tokens that produce each crop. The authors report consistent gains for Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3-VL-8B. They describe OPO-8B as competitive against much larger models and tool-augmented baselines. They present observation policy optimization as an important direction for active visual reasoning.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The conclusion argues that optimizing observation actions directly improves Qwen3-VL-2B and 8B on high-resolution benchmarks.

sections.body: Appendix A gives the clipped PPO objective, with tool-observation tokens masked out of the policy loss. Appendix B describes V* with 191 examples and HR-Bench 4K and 8K, each expanded to 800 evaluation rows. Appendix C specifies greedy decoding with up to 10 tool-use turns. Appendix D reports about 47K training samples from DeepEyes' data recipe. Appendix E gives the tool-call format, and Appendix F gives the reward judges. Appendix G presents qualitative cases, and Appendix H the implementation settings. Appendix I reports that localization failures account for 41 of 50 unsuccessful trajectories in three stronger models. Appendix J states limits: a single zoom tool and only 2B and 8B backbones. Appendix K covers societal impacts.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists the algorithm, benchmarks, training data, prompts, judges, qualitative cases, localization failures and limitations.
